watches.name: Uriel_VII (Blue)
watches.description: More. By Design. MAKINA re-envisions the model that began it all. Uriel returns with Uriel_VII featuring a more refined case and a dial that says more with MAKINA’s first ever full calendar functionality. Now available, Uriel_VII ships with no import fees for customers in the United States and the Philippines, a direct result of our expanded distribution hubs. Controlled Curvature Uriel_VII retains its curvaceous cushion case, now sharpened with more deliberate, defined edges. At 38mm in diameter, 44mm lug-to-lug, and 12.9mm thick, its proportions remain balanced and composed. The brushed mid-case slopes decisively into the caseback, slimming its profile, improving ergonomics and allowing it to wear even more compact on the wrist than its measurements suggest. Brushed and polished surfaces articulate the geometry of the case and separation of its parts. A sapphire crystal crowns the structure with clarity and resilience. Paired with a blue canvas strap, its woven surface adds texture while reinforcing the watch’s utilitarian character and grounded presence on the wrist. Beyond the Three-Hand form The asymmetrical blue dial carries a restrained satin grain, shifting between blue and deep blue as light moves across its surface. Faceted hour indices and sharply defined alpha hands rise from the dial, introducing dimension that feels constructed rather than applied. High-contrast white chapter rings cut decisively through the dark base, framing Uriel’s first full calendar display: day at 9 o’clock, month at 3, and date at 6. The calendar is set within deeply recessed subdials, their stepped architecture creating pronounced vertical separation. Leaf hands sweep across these recessed planes, asserting clarity without compromising its sculptural presence. Born with Mechanical Backbone. Uriel_VII is powered by the Miyota 9122, a proven, reliable workhorse chosen for its stability and practicality. Operating at 28,800 beats per hour (4Hz), it delivers hours, minutes, seconds, day, date, and month functionality, with hacking seconds for precise time-setting. A unidirectional rotor winds the movement efficiently, ensuring dependable performance beneath the surface. Specifications CASE: 33 x 44mm (lug to lug) x 11.5 (thickness), surgical grade stainless steel case. DIAL: Multi-layered brass dial, lumed. Fine sand textured finish. GLASS: High quality, scratch resistant flat sapphire crystal with 3x anti-reflective coating. MOVEMENT: Swiss automatic movement, Sellita SW260-1, 28,800 beats per hour (4Hz). 42-hour power reserve, with hacking seconds. STRAP: Blue canvas strap WATERPROOFING: 50 m rating,

watches.name: Azazel_I Green
watches.description: MAKINA Azazel_I: Built for daily wear. Ready for whatever survives it. A case silhouette like no other: sandblasted, raw, and ready. Its dial breaks from the familiar. A unidirectional timing bezel. Upgraded water resistance. This is Makina’s only demon that’s built for wear, for impact, for whatever’s ahead. A watch that looks as if it’s already been through something... and came out stronger. Raw Geometry. Tough Skin. No Excuses. Made of surgical-grade 316L stainless steel, its case design is like nothing else we’ve made — raw, sculptural, and finished in a rough sandblasted texture that hides scratches and feels carved from something out of this world. Utilitarian but contemporary in design, it’s built to look like it belongs in hostile territory, not behind glass. The unidirectional bezel turns with 120 crisp, mechanical clicks — the kind that feel deliberate, not decorative. With 200 meters of water resistance, this is a watch made to push your everyday frontiers, not just survive them. The domed sapphire crystal is treated with a triple-layer anti-reflective coating, keeping visibility sharp from any angle. And paired with a durable silicone strap, Azazel_I stays comfortable for longer hauls — wherever you’re headed. The Dial: part architecture, part artifact. Geometric and unconventional in its layout, it plays with layered surfaces and negative space to create something familiar, but not quite. At its center, a rotating disc serves as a seconds indicator — a quiet, continuous motion that adds to the dial’s sense of depth and tension. New hand designs debut here, hinting at what’s to come in future Makina models. And with luminous detailing throughout, Azazel_I stays visible when the light disappears — because not everything ends at sundown. The Machine inside the Machine. Inside Azazel_I is the Sellita SW260-1 — a Swiss automatic movement with a small seconds display that powers the rotating disc at 6 o’clock. Operating at 28,800 beats per hour, it offers smooth motion, a 38-hour power reserve, and modern essentials like hacking and hand-winding. Reliable, precise, and built to last — it’s the mechanical heartbeat of a watch that’s made to be worn hard.

watches.name: M33
watches.description: Zero is just the beginning - from M33 by Makina, pronounced "M-Thirty-Three". ​ Zero is clean and minimalist in approach but will grace wrists with unlimited style and Charisma. Zero is unisex. It is the thinnest watch we've buit at only 7.5mm thick and looks even thinner on the wrist due to its unusual saucer-shaped case design. It is 38mm in diameter and made of surgical grade 316L stainless steel. Under the scratch resistant sapphire crystal glass is a dial made of quality metal, painted red with high gloss finish giving the watch lots of funk. CASE: 38mm 316L stainless steel. 7.5mm total thickness. Polished and brushed finish. ​ DIAL: minimalist dial design made of brass with gloss finish. GLASS: high quality, scratch resistant sapphire crystal with 3x anti-reflective coating. ​ MOVEMENT: Quartz movement STRAP: Solid steel bracelet Waterproofing: 50 m rating, ​

watches.name: Andras_II (Black)
watches.description: Refined. Ready. Within Reach Again. Andras II returns with sharper refinements. A new evolution of Makina’s rectangular machine. Pre-orders are now open with a shorter window and reduced pricing. For customers in the USA and the Philippines, delivery comes with NO IMPORT FEES - a direct benefit of our new distribution hubs. Orders placed today will ship between October 15–31. The pre-order window is limited, will close once capacity is reached, and may end without notice. Specifications CASE: 33 x 44mm (lug to lug) x 11.5 (thickness), surgical grade stainless steel case. DIAL: Multi-layered brass dial, lumed. Fine sand textured finish. GLASS: High quality, scratch resistant flat sapphire crystal with 3x anti-reflective coating. MOVEMENT: Swiss automatic movement, Sellita SW260-1, 28,800 beats per hour (4Hz). 42-hour power reserve, with hacking seconds. STRAP: Silicone strap WATERPROOFING: 50 m rating, A Case Carved in Shadow and Steel Sharp. Geometric. Multi-faceted. Architecture reduced to wrist form. Brushed planes and polished edges shift with the light, every angle cut with purpose. Updated with a bevelled bezel sharpening form and fit. Forged from surgical-grade stainless steel and cloaked in pitch-black PVD, the case is as tough as it is sculptural. At 33 × 44 mm, it wears compact yet commanding, sealed beneath scratch-resistant sapphire. This isn’t just a shell for timekeeping; it’s armor for the machine inside. A Framed Industrial Landscape Its dial doesn’t just tell time — it plays with light and depth. Its multi-layered construction creates shifting shadows across the surface, pulling the eye inward. A sand-textured finish grounds the design in raw, tactile grit — a surface that feels alive under changing light. Faceted hour markers, hand-polished to catch every angle, rise like architectural beams. The hands are stripped back, sharper, more modern — each tipped with a flash of electric blue that cuts through the black. Even the recessed sub-dial feels carved, not placed, adding another tier of dimensionality. This is not an ordinary flat dial; it’s a dark landscape. The Engine Room Andras_II runs on the Swiss-made SW260-1 automatic movement — a workhorse built for reliability, precision, and everyday endurance. It drives the essentials: hours, minutes, and seconds, beating at 28,800 vibrations per hour, wound by a bidirectional rotor that feeds on every movement of the wrist. Through the exhibition-style caseback, it bears Makina’s gold-plated rotor — the lone signature on a proven machine.

watches.name: MAKINA GABRIEL_I Salmon
watches.description: What you see here is a hand polished 40mm case made of 316L stainless steel with an angular, octagonal silhouette and a water resistance rating of 100 meters. Handsome and dressy at only 11.9mm thick. In striking contrast with the rounded off sides, the top and bottom surfaces are completely flat with wire lugs connecting them to the navy blue, genuine crocodile strap. Intentionally designed to have no number indicators for simplicity, the two tone dial under the domed sapphire crystal glass is our modern take on the classic sector dial in salmon color. The accented blue plated hands are gem-cut and made of brass. The railway minute track surrounds a circular satin-brushed chapter ring highlighting the embossed hour markers. Decorated with a circular guilloche, this is the first time we've ever incorporated a seconds sub dial on any of our dials. The sub dial is intentionally marker-less - we feel that with dress watches, most people don't really read time with accuracy down to seconds, let alone on a small sub dial that is often difficult to read. So here, the sub dial is purely for aesthetics and serves as an indicator of whether or not the movement is still powered. On the back is an exhibition style case back with a blue tinted window looking into the renowned and highly reliable Sellita SW 260-1 that powers the watch with a 38 hour power reserve.

watches.name: MAKINAxQUICCS
watches.description: COLLECTIBLE ART IN WRIST FORM QUICCS is one of the most influential voices in the global designer toy movement, renowned for a visual universe shaped by street art, contemporary pop culture, and collectible design. For this special edition, MAKINA's design-driven approach to watchmaking provides the canvas for QUICCS' unmistakable artistic language, with his iconic Manila Killa serving as the centerpiece of the watch. Released in celebration of Philippine Independence Day, this special edition pays tribute to a new generation of Filipino creativity—where art, design, and culture intersect. ​ For this release, distribution will be handled separately by territory. MAKINA will serve customers in the United States, while QUICCS will oversee distribution within the Philippines. ITS GEOMETRIC FRAME ​ Forged from surgical-grade stainless steel, Andras_II balances sharp lines, faceted surfaces, brushed textures, and polished accents in a form where meticulous hand-finishing meets machine-made precision. Measuring 33 × 44 mm and protected by scratch-resistant sapphire, its architectural profile provides the perfect stage for the protagonist within. Included are three interchangeable rubber straps in red, white, and yellow, allowing the watch to take on a different personality with each change. A MACHINE'S PORTRAIT Beneath sapphire crystal, QUICCS' Manila Killa occupies center stage, elevated above the dial surface and bringing physical depth to graphic illustration. Created using a multi-layer UV printing process, the artwork is gradually built up rather than simply printed, introducing texture, shadow, and dimension throughout the composition. As light moves across the dial, the raised surfaces reveal subtle details and contours that conventional printing cannot achieve. Drawing from the colors of the Philippine flag, the hands introduce flashes of red and blue, while a yellow sword-shaped seconds hand sweeps across the dial. What begins as illustration becomes object, with the dial bringing one of QUICCS' most recognizable creations to life, making collectible art wearable art. ITS MECHANICAL HEART . Beneath the artwork lies the Miyota 8215 automatic movement, a long-standing Japanese caliber respected for its reliability and straightforward serviceability. Featuring automatic winding, central seconds, and date functionality, it provides the mechanical foundation for daily wear. While the artwork commands attention, the movement quietly performs its role behind the scenes—keeping the piece in motion, one sweep at a time.​ SPECIFICATIONS WARRANTY: 2 Years CASE: 33mm x 44mm (lug to lug) x 11.3mm (thickness), 316L surgical grade stainless steel. Hand-brushed, hand-polished finishing. DIAL: Double-layer brass dial featuring raised multi-layer UV-printed artwork. GLASS: High quality, scratch resistant flat sapphire crystal with 3x anti-reflective coating. MOVEMENT: Japanese automatic movement, Miyota 8215, 21,600 beats per hour (3Hz). 42-hour power reserve, with central seconds, and bi-directional automatic winding. STRAP: Rubber strap (red, white, yellow) WATERPROOFING: 50 m rating,

watches.name: MEPHISTO_III GMT (Blue)
watches.description: MAKINA Mephisto III GMT: MAKINA’s First Design Reimagined for the World Traveler MAKINA Watches is pleased to introduce MAKINA Mephisto III GMT, an evolution of the brand’s inaugural design, launched in 2017, now enhanced with a GMT complication that offers global travelers and watch enthusiasts precision and style across any time zone. By blending MAKINA’s sculpted design language with a customized movement from Miyota’s premium line, this timepiece reflects our continued commitment to originality and functionality in a more refined, integrated package. Every Surface Counts: The Intricate Finishing of Mephisto III GMT The Mephisto III GMT features a 38mm case crafted from surgical-grade 316L stainless steel, with a 45mm lug-to-lug distance and a case thickness of 11.55mm. Polished concave edges on the case, bezel, and case back flow seamlessly into MAKINA’s first integrated bracelet design, resulting in a cohesive, sculpted aesthetic. This model showcases our most intricate case design to date, thoughtfully crafted to achieve a harmonious interplay of brushed and polished finishes—a challenge made even more demanding by the small, intricately designed surfaces of the case that must be meticulously polished by hand. Four Hands. Two Timezones. Beneath the sapphire crystal glass with a triple-layer anti-reflective coating lies a newly redesigned, multifaceted dial with sloping surfaces in blue, adding even greater depth and dimension. Inspired by the original Mephisto, this evolution features multiple layers, tall metallic indices, and faceted alpha hands, creating a dynamic interplay of light with every wrist movement. The stainless steel-colored outer ring, finished with a refined brushed texture, integrates seamlessly with the bezel and prominently displays a 24-hour scale in red, enhancing separation, improving visibility, and establishing a clear visual connection to the matching red GMT hand. The Heart of The Machine At the heart of Mephisto III GMT is the Miyota 9075 automatic movement, a reliable GMT caliber that allows for independent adjustment of the local hour hand. Visible through an exhibition case back, the movement features Côtes de Genève finishing and is customized with MAKINA’s gold electroplated rotor, adding a subtle touch of elegance to mechanical precision. Operating at a high frequency of 28,800 beats per hour (4Hz), it offers a 42-hour power reserve, along with hacking seconds for precise time setting.

watches.description: After 7 years, Mephisto is back One of the things that gives the architecture of Mephisto_III a unique appearance is that its case is angular as a whole but embellished with curvaceous and highly polished concave edges everywhere from bezel, case, crown, case back to the integrated bracelet that give its silhouette multiple levels and finishes making this Makina’s most detailed case design yet. Its sharp edges are crisp with clear cut, alternating brushed and polished finishing. One of the reasons the release of this model has been delayed multiple times is the meticulous effort in craftsmanship involved in producing the concave edges found in its integrated bracelet which connects seamlessly to the watch case. ​ The 38mm case is made of surgical grade, 316L stainless steel and measures at only 45mm lug to lug and case thickness of 11.15 mm. The crown is a screw down type with a 100m water resistance rating. Under the highly scratch resistant flat sapphire crystal glass with 3x AR coating is a dial design inspired by the very first Mephisto, the very first model to come out of Makina, but has grown to become even more multifaceted allowing for more light play during wrist rolls. The dial’s multi-layered design, its tall metallic indexes and faceted alpha hands add 3-dimensional interest not commonly found in 3-handed timepieces. The exhibition style case back displays the highly renowned, Swiss-made, Sellita SW200 movement modified with a gold electro-plated rotor. The movement has a power reserve of 38 hours with a beat rate of 28,800 bph with hacking seconds. Specification Summary CASE: 38mm, surgical grade stainless steel case. Only 45mm lug to lug and only 11.15mm total thickness. ​ CROWN: Screw down ​ DIAL: Multi-faceted brass dial with thick metallic indices and brass faceted hands. GLASS: High quality, scratch resistant sapphire crystal with 3x anti-reflective coating. ​ MOVEMENT: Modified, automatic Swiss made Sellita SW200 with 26 Jewels with hacking seconds, 41 hr power reserve. watches.name: MAKINA RAUM_I White
watches.description: Built like a tank made of 316L stainless steel, Raum is made for prominence even when measuring only at 42mm in diameter, 48mm lug to lug. An angular design at first glance but is actually curvaceous in totality, brushed and polished in alternating surfaces. Underneath the sapphire crystal...​ is a very 3 dimensional dial with embossed metallic markers for odd hours and with even hours represented by concave shapes carved into the brass made dial. We opted to go with gold plated brass hands that we think add character to the entire piece... plus, it matches what's on the back. On the back... ​is an automatic Sellita SW 200-1 (38 hr power reserve), visible through an exhibition caseback. Raum_I will be the first from Makina to sport a Swiss movement. Apart from the back of the case being uniquely flat, the case construction of Raum is quite different; the traditional circular caseback shape that you see in the photo is actually one piece with the sides and lugs. Raum is dressed in a genuine calf leather strap, hand-made and hand-stitched, with a deployant clasp for convenience and protection of the leather. It is intended to be versatile and can be worn as a sporty dress watch, as well as a rugged daily wear adventurer. ​ Raum will be produced in limited quantities and will be released in small batches.

watches.name: Azazel_I GMT BLK
watches.description: MAKINA Azazel_I GMT: One machine. Two places at once. The Azazel_I GMT takes Makina’s most rugged form somewhere new. Its unmistakable sandblasted case surrounds a deeply layered dial, now reworked to track a second time zone without surrendering the unconventional architecture that defines the collection. A unidirectional timing bezel, increased water resistance, and a robust japanese automatic movement give it the substance to match its presence. Made for changing cities, shifting hours, and whatever comes in between. The Rougher Side of Refinement. The Azazel_I GMT is wrapped in 316L stainless steel, shaped into a case that feels equal parts machine and armor. Its rough sandblasted surface gives the metal a raw, almost stone-like character — while helping hide the scratches and marks that come with daily wear. It’s tough by design, but never at the expense of the details that matter. The unidirectional bezel moves through 120 firm, mechanical clicks, while 200 meters of water resistance means the Azazel_I GMT is ready for considerably more than the journey between airports. A domed sapphire crystal with triple-layer anti-reflective coating keeps the dial clear through changing light and unfamiliar surroundings. Finished with a durable rubber strap built for comfort over long hours, it’s made for the kind of wear that leaves a story, not a scar. Familiar Function. Unfamiliar Form. At its center sits the GMT disc, rotating to track a second time zone. A circular aperture cut into the disc points to the corresponding hour on the 24-hour scale hidden below — transforming a familiar GMT complication into something distinctly Makina. That same aperture doubles as a day/night indicator: orange signals the sun and daylight in the second time zone, while white becomes the moon, marking the arrival of night. The Azazel_I GMT maintains Makina’s signature two-pronged hour and minute hands, now joined by a central seconds hand. At 3 o’clock, the dial tapers inward to reveal the date display, integrating another function into the dial’s layered architecture rather than simply placing a window on its surface. Luminous detailing across the dial and hands provides greater visibility in low light, keeping its information readable when daylight disappears. The Engine Behind the GMT Inside the Azazel_I GMT is the Miyota 9075, a Japanese automatic movement built around true GMT functionality. Its independently adjustable local hour hand lets you change time zones without disturbing the minutes, seconds, or GMT indication — a practical complication made for movement. Operating at 28,800 beats per hour, it delivers a smooth sweep, approximately 42 hours of power reserve, and modern essentials including hacking and hand-winding. Robust, reliable, and purpose-built for travel — it’s the mechanical engine behind Azazel_I GMT’s new way of keeping time.

watches.name: MAKINA ANDRAS_I Gray
watches.description: Introducing, our stealthiest yet, Makina Andras_I - our first rectangular watch and watch case in PVD coated surgical grade 316L stainless steel. In an industry where rectangular watches are almost always art deco inspired dress watches, Andras_I is designed to be sportier and more contemporary. Although it is only 44mm lug to lug, 33mm wide and 10,5mm thick, Andras_I packs a lot of wrist presence. The case is shapely and multi-faceted with both round and sharp edges. watches.name: Azazel_I Black
watches.description: MAKINA Azazel_I: Built for daily wear. Ready for whatever survives it. A case silhouette like no other: sandblasted, raw, and ready. Its dial breaks from the familiar. A unidirectional timing bezel. Upgraded water resistance. This is Makina’s only demon that’s built for wear, for impact, for whatever’s ahead. A watch that looks as if it’s already been through something... and came out stronger. Raw Geometry. Tough Skin. No Excuses. Made of surgical-grade 316L stainless steel, its case design is like nothing else we’ve made — raw, sculptural, and finished in a rough sandblasted texture that hides scratches and feels carved from something out of this world. Utilitarian but contemporary in design, it’s built to look like it belongs in hostile territory, not behind glass. The unidirectional bezel turns with 120 crisp, mechanical clicks — the kind that feel deliberate, not decorative. With 200 meters of water resistance, this is a watch made to push your everyday frontiers, not just survive them. The domed sapphire crystal is treated with a triple-layer anti-reflective coating, keeping visibility sharp from any angle. And paired with a durable silicone strap, Azazel_I stays comfortable for longer hauls — wherever you’re headed. The Dial: part architecture, part artifact. Geometric and unconventional in its layout, it plays with layered surfaces and negative space to create something familiar, but not quite. At its center, a rotating disc serves as a seconds indicator — a quiet, continuous motion that adds to the dial’s sense of depth and tension. New hand designs debut here, hinting at what’s to come in future Makina models. And with luminous detailing throughout, Azazel_I stays visible when the light disappears — because not everything ends at sundown. The Machine inside the Machine. Inside Azazel_I is the Sellita SW260-1 — a Swiss automatic movement with a small seconds display that powers the rotating disc at 6 o’clock. Operating at 28,800 beats per hour, it offers smooth motion, a 38-hour power reserve, and modern essentials like hacking and hand-winding. Reliable, precise, and built to last — it’s the mechanical heartbeat of a watch that’s made to be worn hard.

watches.name: Cassiel_II
watches.description: A Refined Industrial Machine. Cassiel_II is MAKINA’s newest flagship - a mechanical artifact from a future not yet written. As the brand’s first timepiece with an automatic chronograph function, it treats the complication not as a nostalgic motorsport reference, but as a study in industrial form. Built around an entirely new case geometry, the watch balances rough sandblasted planes with polished accents, giving its angular body visual weight and refinement. Cassiel_II rejects the familiar order of traditional dial configurations, replacing flat registers with layered displays and rotating elements that appear embedded within the object itself. Monolithic in presence yet refined in expression, it becomes a contemporary piece of industrial machinery disciplined into wrist-worn form.

watches.name: MAKINA RAUM_I
watches.description: Built like a tank made of 316L stainless steel, Raum is made for prominence even when measuring only at 42mm in diameter, 48mm lug to lug. An angular design at first glance but is actually curvaceous in totality, brushed and polished in alternating surfaces. Underneath the sapphire crystal...​ is a very 3 dimensional dial with embossed metallic markers for odd hours and with even hours represented by concave shapes carved into the brass made dial. We opted to go with gold plated brass hands that we think add character to the entire piece... plus, it matches what's on the back. On the back... ​is an automatic Sellita SW 200-1 (38 hr power reserve), visible through an exhibition caseback. Raum_I will be the first from Makina to sport a Swiss movement. Apart from the back of the case being uniquely flat, the case construction of Raum is quite different; the traditional circular caseback shape that you see in the photo is actually one piece with the sides and lugs. Raum is dressed in a genuine crocodile leather strap, hand-made and hand-stitched, with a deployant clasp for convenience and protection of the leather. It is intended to be versatile and can be worn as a sporty dress watch, as well as a rugged daily wear adventurer. ​ Raum will be produced in limited quantities and will be released in small batches.

watches.name: Uriel_VII (Black)
watches.description: More. By Design. MAKINA re-envisions the model that began it all. Uriel returns with Uriel_VII featuring a more refined case and a dial that says more with MAKINA’s first ever full calendar functionality. Now available, Uriel_VII ships with no import fees for customers in the United States and the Philippines, a direct result of our expanded distribution hubs. Controlled Curvature Uriel_VII retains its curvaceous cushion case, now sharpened with more deliberate, defined edges. At 38mm in diameter, 44mm lug-to-lug, and 12.9mm thick, its proportions remain balanced and composed. The brushed mid-case slopes decisively into the caseback, slimming its profile, improving ergonomics and allowing it to wear even more compact on the wrist than its measurements suggest. Brushed and polished surfaces articulate the geometry of the case and separation of its parts. A sapphire crystal crowns the structure with clarity and resilience. Paired with a black canvas strap, its woven surface adds texture while reinforcing the watch’s utilitarian character and grounded presence on the wrist. Beyond the Three-Hand form The asymmetrical black dial carries a restrained satin grain, shifting between charcoal and deep black as light moves across its surface. Faceted hour indices and sharply defined alpha hands rise from the dial, introducing dimension that feels constructed rather than applied. High-contrast white chapter rings cut decisively through the dark base, framing Uriel’s first full calendar display: day at 9 o’clock, month at 3, and date at 6. The calendar is set within deeply recessed subdials, their stepped architecture creating pronounced vertical separation. Leaf hands sweep across these recessed planes, asserting clarity without compromising its sculptural presence. Born with Mechanical Backbone. Uriel_VII is powered by the Miyota 9122, a proven, reliable workhorse chosen for its stability and practicality. Operating at 28,800 beats per hour (4Hz), it delivers hours, minutes, seconds, day, date, and month functionality, with hacking seconds for precise time-setting. A unidirectional rotor winds the movement efficiently, ensuring dependable performance beneath the surface. Specifications CASE: 33 x 44mm (lug to lug) x 11.5 (thickness), surgical grade stainless steel case. DIAL: Multi-layered brass dial, lumed. Fine sand textured finish. GLASS: High quality, scratch resistant flat sapphire crystal with 3x anti-reflective coating. MOVEMENT: Swiss automatic movement, Sellita SW260-1, 28,800 beats per hour (4Hz). 42-hour power reserve, with hacking seconds. STRAP: Silicone strap WATERPROOFING: 50 m rating, A Case Carved in Shadow and Steel

watches.name: MEPHISTO_III GMT (Gray)
watches.description: MAKINA Mephisto III GMT: MAKINA’s First Design Reimagined for the World Traveler MAKINA Watches is pleased to introduce MAKINA Mephisto III GMT, an evolution of the brand’s inaugural design, launched in 2017, now enhanced with a GMT complication that offers global travelers and watch enthusiasts precision and style across any time zone. By blending MAKINA’s sculpted design language with a customized movement from Miyota’s premium line, this timepiece reflects our continued commitment to originality and functionality in a more refined, integrated package. Every Surface Counts: The Intricate Finishing of Mephisto III GMT The Mephisto III GMT features a 38mm case crafted from surgical-grade 316L stainless steel, with a 45mm lug-to-lug distance and a case thickness of 11.55mm. Polished concave edges on the case, bezel, and case back flow seamlessly into MAKINA’s first integrated bracelet design, resulting in a cohesive, sculpted aesthetic. This model showcases our most intricate case design to date, thoughtfully crafted to achieve a harmonious interplay of brushed and polished finishes—a challenge made even more demanding by the small, intricately designed surfaces of the case that must be meticulously polished by hand. Four Hands. Two Timezones. Beneath the sapphire crystal glass with a triple-layer anti-reflective coating lies a newly redesigned, multifaceted dial with sloping surfaces in blue, adding even greater depth and dimension. Inspired by the original Mephisto, this evolution features multiple layers, tall metallic indices, and faceted alpha hands, creating a dynamic interplay of light with every wrist movement. The stainless steel-colored outer ring, finished with a refined brushed texture, integrates seamlessly with the bezel and prominently displays a 24-hour scale in red, enhancing separation, improving visibility, and establishing a clear visual connection to the matching red GMT hand. The Heart of The Machine At the heart of Mephisto III GMT is the Miyota 9075 automatic movement, a reliable GMT caliber that allows for independent adjustment of the local hour hand. Visible through an exhibition case back, the movement features Côtes de Genève finishing and is customized with MAKINA’s gold electroplated rotor, adding a subtle touch of elegance to mechanical precision. Operating at a high frequency of 28,800 beats per hour (4Hz), it offers a 42-hour power reserve, along with hacking seconds for precise time setting.

The crown is a screw down type with a 100m water resistance rating. Under the highly scratch resistant flat sapphire crystal glass with 3x AR coating is a dial design inspired by the very first Mephisto, the very first model to come out of Makina, but has grown to become even more multifaceted allowing for more light play during wrist rolls. watches.name: MAKINA GABRIEL_I
watches.description: What you see here is a hand polished 40mm case made of 316L stainless steel with an angular, octagonal silhouette and a water resistance rating of 100 meters. Handsome and dressy at only 11.9mm thick. In striking contrast with the rounded off sides, the top and bottom surfaces are completely flat with wire lugs connecting them to the navy blue, genuine crocodile strap. Intentionally designed to have no number indicators for simplicity, the two tone dial under the domed sapphire crystal glass is our modern take on the classic sector dial. The accented blue plated hands are gem-cut and made of brass. The railway minute track surrounds a circular satin-brushed chapter ring highlighting the embossed hour markers. Decorated with a circular guilloche, this is the first time we've ever incorporated a seconds sub dial on any of our dials. The sub dial is intentionally marker-less - we feel that with dress watches, most people don't really read time with accuracy down to seconds, let alone on a small sub dial that is often difficult to read. So here, the sub dial is purely for aesthetics and serves as an indicator of whether or not the movement is still powered. On the back is an exhibition style case back with a blue tinted window looking into the renowned and highly reliable Sellita SW 260-1 that powers the watch with a 38 hour power reserve.

watches.name: Azazel_I GMT Blue
watches.description: MAKINA Azazel_I GMT: One machine. Two places at once. The Azazel_I GMT takes Makina’s most rugged form somewhere new. Its unmistakable sandblasted case surrounds a deeply layered dial, now reworked to track a second time zone without surrendering the unconventional architecture that defines the collection. A unidirectional timing bezel, increased water resistance, and a robust japanese automatic movement give it the substance to match its presence. Made for changing cities, shifting hours, and whatever comes in between. The Rougher Side of Refinement. The Azazel_I GMT is wrapped in 316L stainless steel, shaped into a case that feels equal parts machine and armor. Its rough sandblasted surface gives the metal a raw, almost stone-like character — while helping hide the scratches and marks that come with daily wear. It’s tough by design, but never at the expense of the details that matter. The unidirectional bezel moves through 120 firm, mechanical clicks, while 200 meters of water resistance means the Azazel_I GMT is ready for considerably more than the journey between airports. A domed sapphire crystal with triple-layer anti-reflective coating keeps the dial clear through changing light and unfamiliar surroundings. Finished with a durable rubber strap built for comfort over long hours, it’s made for the kind of wear that leaves a story, not a scar. Familiar Function. Unfamiliar Form. At its center sits the GMT disc, rotating to track a second time zone. A circular aperture cut into the disc points to the corresponding hour on the 24-hour scale hidden below — transforming a familiar GMT complication into something distinctly Makina. That same aperture doubles as a day/night indicator: orange signals the sun and daylight in the second time zone, while white becomes the moon, marking the arrival of night. The Azazel_I GMT maintains Makina’s signature two-pronged hour and minute hands, now joined by a central seconds hand. At 3 o’clock, the dial tapers inward to reveal the date display, integrating another function into the dial’s layered architecture rather than simply placing a window on its surface. Luminous detailing across the dial and hands provides greater visibility in low light, keeping its information readable when daylight disappears. The Engine Behind the GMT Inside the Azazel_I GMT is the Miyota 9075, a Japanese automatic movement built around true GMT functionality. Its independently adjustable local hour hand lets you change time zones without disturbing the minutes, seconds, or GMT indication — a practical complication made for movement. Operating at 28,800 beats per hour, it delivers a smooth sweep, approximately 42 hours of power reserve, and modern essentials including hacking and hand-winding. Robust, reliable, and purpose-built for travel — it’s the mechanical engine behind Azazel_I GMT’s new way of keeping time.
